titleStmt.title: SUGGESTED LETTER TO PRESIDENT DE LA GUARDIA

div.head: SUGGESTED LETTER TO PRESIDENT DE LA GUARDIA
div.p: Since receiving your letter of March seventh, I have given careful consideration to the course of relations between our two countries. I have been particularly encouraged to receive recent information that our representatives have been making progress toward reducing points of divergence in the application of the Treaty of Mutual Understanding and Cooperation of 1955.

The pending issues between our two countries arising in the course of implementation of that Treaty have been and are under continuing study by the responsible officers of this Government, including myself. It is clear to me by now that further discussion of the intent and meaning of certain aspects of our Treaty undertaking is unlikely
to bring about full agreement. However, I do not think that this should deter our efforts to achieve over-increasing understanding between one and two countries. For my part, accordingly, I have approved a number of revisions in operating policies of the Canal Zone authorities
which result from a meeting of representatives of our two Governments in which you actively participated. I trust that these actions, the substance of which will be communicated to you by Ambassador Harrington, will redound to the benefit of the people of Panama.

I am confident that it is your desire, as it is mine, that our two countries should continue their traditionally close cooperation to insure the efficient operation of the Panama Canal for the benefit of the entire world.

note.p: Drafted by Sharp on October 21, approved in draft by Assistant Secretary of State Rubottom and Assistant Secretary of the Army Roderick, and approved in substance by Ambassador Harrington.

In view of the riots that occurred in Panama City on November 3, 1959, Ambassador Harrington, in the course of a telephone conversation on November 4 with C. Allen Stewart, the Director of the Office of Central American and Panamanian Affairs, recommended against delivery on November 5 of President Eisenhower’s letter to President de la Guardia. Stewart accepted Harrington’s recommendation and advised the Ambassador that the Department would furnish the Embassy with instructions as to further action concerning delivery of the President’s letter. (Memorandum of Telephone Conversation, by Frederick D. Sharp III, November 4; 719.00/11–459) on November 4, the Department instructed Harrington to return the President’s letter to the Department via air pouch. (Telegram 151 to Panama City; 719.11–459) For additional information concerning the riots in Panama City on November 3, see the editorial note, in Document PM–23.
